claim: All four built-in remote-provider adapters accept bounded custom-function definitions and normalize provider function calls into one transient inspect-only proposal lifecycle without adding tool execution, result continuation, or ambient application authority.
commands: node scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- cargo test --manifest-path frontend/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib provider_ -- --nocapture
node scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- npm --prefix frontend run build
node scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- npm --prefix frontend run check:supervised
proved: OpenAI/xAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, and Gemini Interactions receive their provider-specific custom-function definition shapes from one validated provider-neutral request.
Definitions require unique bounded names, printable bounded descriptions, and a bounded JSON-object parameter schema rooted at type object.
OpenAI argument deltas, Anthropic partial_json blocks, Gemini complete function-call steps, and xAI whole-call chunks normalize into the same start/delta/complete proposal lifecycle.

Call count, call IDs, names, per-call arguments, aggregate arguments, event order, and final JSON equality are bounded and checked independently in the provider decoder, runtime accumulator, and frontend reducer.
Orphaned, duplicate, mismatched, malformed, non-object, oversized, truncated, or unfinished calls fail closed in hostile synthetic fixtures.
The native disclosure derives a category for tool names, descriptions, and argument schemas from the actual request rather than trusting caller-authored disclosure metadata.
The workspace labels calls inspect only and not executed, offers no Run tool control, retains proposals only in transient state, and never applies them to the shared draft.
The content-free provider-run record stores no response text or tool-argument body; its outputSha256 commits to both normalized text and proposals.
No test or runtime path gave a proposal MCP, Drive, filesystem, plugin, editor, network, or shared-project mutation authority.
notProved: Any live OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or xAI model, credential, provider response shape, rate limit, billing behavior, retention policy, or server-side tool behavior.
Validation of returned arguments against the supplied JSON Schema or any domain-specific semantic validator.
Tool execution, tool-result transmission, multi-turn continuation, retry, idempotency, permission brokering, or user approval for a concrete tool authority.
Built-in provider tools, remote MCP tools, Drive access, filesystem access, plugin execution, editor mutation, network access, or shared-project mutation.
Slow-consumer or backpressure behavior, packaged native Send once dialog interaction, or a shipped updater artifact containing this checkpoint.
Any model-quality, truth, safety, consensus, feature-parity, or superiority property.
